mcqs.question: In the figure, O is the centre of a circle and P is a point on the circle. Which of the following line segments represents the radius of the circle?
mcqs.explanation: A radius is a line segment joining the centre of a circle to any point on the circle. Segment OP connects centre O to point P on the circle, so it is the radius. OA and OC are not defined as radii unless A or C lie on the circle, and PA does not involve the centre.

mcqs.question: A straight line passes through the centre O of a circle and meets the circle at points A and B. Which segment is the diameter of the circle?
mcqs.explanation: A diameter is a chord that passes through the centre of the circle. The segment AB joins the two points where the line through O meets the circle, so AB is the diameter. OA and OB are radii, not diameters, and OC is unrelated.

mcqs.question: Which of the following statements about a chord is FALSE?

options.A: Every chord has both its endpoints on the circle.
options.B: A diameter is a special type of chord.
options.C: All chords must pass through the centre of the circle.
options.D: A chord can be shorter than the radius.

mcqs.answer: All chords must pass through the centre of the circle.
mcqs.explanation: A chord is any segment whose endpoints lie on the circle. Only the diameter passes through the centre; other chords do not. Therefore statement C is false. Statements A, B, and D are true.

mcqs.question: In a circle, points X and Y lie on the circumference. The shorter part of the circle joining X and Y is called the:
mcqs.explanation: The part of the circumference between two points that is less than half the circle is the minor arc. The longer part is the major arc. A chord is a straight line, and a diameter must pass through the centre, which is not implied here.

mcqs.question: Which of the following correctly describes the circumference of a circle?

options.A: It is the area enclosed by the circle.
options.B: It is the distance around the circle, equal to 2πr.
options.C: It is the line segment joining two points on the circle through the centre.
options.D: It is the radius multiplied by the diameter.

mcqs.answer: It is the distance around the circle, equal to 2πr.
mcqs.explanation: Circumference is the perimeter of a circle, given by 2πr (or πd). Option A describes area, C describes a diameter, and D is not a standard formula.

mcqs.learning_point: Understand the relationship between radius and diameter
mcqs.question: If the radius of a circle is r, which of the following statements is always true?
mcqs.explanation: By definition, the diameter of a circle is twice its radius (d = 2r). The other options misuse the relationship.

mcqs.question: Which point is the centre of a circle?

options.A: The point equidistant from all points on the circumference.

mcqs.answer: The point equidistant from all points on the circumference.
mcqs.explanation: The centre is defined as the unique point that is at the same distance (the radius) from every point on the circle. Option D also describes the centre but is less direct; the most precise definition is option A.

mcqs.question: In a circle with centre O, which of the following statements correctly identifies a radius?

options.A: A line segment joining O to any point on the circle.
options.B: A line segment joining two points on the circle.
options.C: A line segment joining O to the farthest point outside the circle.
options.D: A line segment that bisects a chord.

mcqs.answer: A line segment joining O to any point on the circle.
mcqs.explanation: A radius connects the centre to any point on the circumference. Option B describes a chord, C is unrelated, and D describes a perpendicular bisector of a chord, not a radius.
